closures.observed_problem: The focused traceability reconciliation test rejected the verified UI-11 rows and treated UI-11 as the in-flight phase.
closures.evidence: Phase23TraceabilityTest failed 2 of 15 cases and named all six UI-11 traceability rows.
closures.root_cause: The deterministic lifecycle consumer still listed verified UI phases only through UI-10 and kept P23_IN_FLIGHT_PHASE at UI-11 after PR #61 merged.
closures.why_root_cause: Those two stale constants explain both failures while the live PR, CI, merge and traceability facts agree that UI-11 is verified and UI-12 is active.
closures.correct_fix: Add UI-11 to the verified phase sets, remove it from unverified sets, advance the in-flight phase to UI-12 and remove UI-12 from deferrable phases.
tests: docker compose exec -T app php artisan test tests/Feature/Traceability/Phase23TraceabilityTest.php --compact
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the focused traceability suite passed 15 tests and 20 assertions.

closures.observed_problem: After advancing the in-flight phase, the traceability suite passed assertions but marked the in-flight-phase case risky.
closures.evidence: The focused rerun reported 14 passed and 1 risky because UI-12 has no traceability rows at kickoff.
closures.root_cause: The assertion lived only inside a loop over in-flight rows, so the documented valid zero-row kickoff state executed no assertion.
closures.why_root_cause: UI-11 had rows and masked the harness flaw; advancing to UI-12 made the empty input exercise the zero-assertion path.
closures.correct_fix: Aggregate any premature verified rows and assert once that the resulting list is empty, preserving the invariant for zero or many rows.
tests: docker compose exec -T app php artisan test tests/Feature/Traceability/Phase23TraceabilityTest.php --compact
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the focused traceability suite passed without risky tests.

closures.observed_problem: The Finance account did not resolve the binding 24-destination host-relative contract and reused a legacy task inbox as its dashboard.
closures.evidence: Initial router inspection found only the legacy /finance tree, renamed domain destinations, no dedicated dashboard/tasks split, and no duplicate or partial/split pages.
closures.root_cause: The shipped domain increments delivered Finance workflows independently, but no UI-12 composition had activated the canonical account information architecture.
closures.why_root_cause: The domain routes and authority existed for most destinations while the account router and generated navigation still described legacy or planned ownership.
closures.correct_fix: Compose exactly 20 live host-relative Finance routes, retain only guarded same-account compatibility redirects, and keep the four named Gate W/21N destinations visible but inert.
closures.remaining_risk: External Gate W and Phase 21N remain closed and are explicitly outside UI-12.

closures.observed_problem: The first focused partial/split API test raised a TypeError while eager-loading payment groups.
closures.evidence: The relation eager-load callback received HasMany while the closure was incorrectly narrowed to Eloquent Builder.
closures.root_cause: The eager-load constraint used a query-builder parameter type that did not match Laravel's relationship callback contract.
closures.why_root_cause: Removing the invalid narrow type allowed the same constrained relationship query to execute and the server-derived waterfall assertions to pass.
closures.correct_fix: Use the relationship callback contract without an incompatible Builder type annotation; keep all branch, state and pagination constraints unchanged.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the focused API suite passed 4 tests and 52 assertions.

closures.observed_problem: Visual browser review showed Reporting & Audit and Utility ahead of the Finance workflow groups in the left navigation.
closures.evidence: The initial dashboard screenshot displayed the shared group order instead of Appendix A's seven-group Finance sequence.
closures.root_cause: The shared explicit order appended Finance-only groups after the shared Utility entry.
closures.why_root_cause: All destinations were present, but only the comparator order was wrong; selecting the Finance sequence when Merchant-Client Finance exists produced the binding order without changing predecessor accounts.
closures.correct_fix: Add an explicit Finance seven-group sequence and assert the rendered headings in exact order.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the full focused browser matrix passed with the exact order assertion.

closures.observed_problem: The first browser run rejected Chromium's reduced-motion transition duration even though it was effectively zero.
closures.evidence: Chromium serialized the duration as 0.00001 seconds while the test required the literal string 0s.
closures.root_cause: The assertion tested a browser serialization detail rather than the semantic reduced-motion threshold.
closures.why_root_cause: The computed value was five orders of magnitude below a perceptible animation and the CSS reduced-motion utility was active.
closures.correct_fix: Parse the computed duration and require it to be no greater than 0.00001 seconds.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; reduced motion and all 59 focused browser checks passed.

closures.observed_problem: A frozen-source browser run lost its first dashboard navigation to ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED while the remaining 58 checks passed.
closures.evidence: Only the first page.goto failed; the preview served every subsequent route, width and accessibility case in the same run.
closures.root_cause: The freshly built Vite preview briefly closed its listener during hand-off after Playwright's outer readiness probe.
closures.why_root_cause: A bounded direct readiness probe before product-health listeners eliminated the first-navigation race without filtering any product request, console or page failure.
closures.correct_fix: Probe the preview root for at most five seconds before attaching meaning to browser product-health observations, then rerun the complete suite.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the authoritative focused rerun passed 59/59 in 222.3 seconds.

closures.observed_problem: The shell overview and page-specific duplicate/split loads shared one loading and error channel.
closures.evidence: AppShell starts fetchOverview for branch context while DuplicateReferenceReview and PartialSplitPayments start separate requests on mount; either completion could clear loading or overwrite an unrelated error.
closures.root_cause: The initial UI-12 Pinia store represented three independent network resources with one shared loading/error pair and did not deduplicate concurrent overview consumers.
closures.why_root_cause: A controlled deferred-promise test reproduced simultaneous request states and proves independent channels remain correct regardless of response order.
closures.correct_fix: Separate overview, duplicate and partial/split loading/error channels and reuse one in-flight overview promise between shell and page consumers.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; focused store/page tests passed and the renewed 59-test browser matrix passed in 209.3 seconds.

closures.observed_problem: The deterministic traceability route-parity case rejected five retired Finance route claims.
closures.evidence: The targeted contract run passed 92 cases and failed only the frontend inventory mapping for payment records, platform fees, liabilities, payout runs and earnings queries.
closures.root_cause: Verified backend requirement rows retained pre-UI-12 frontend route names after the canonical Finance account activated replacement routes and removed Finance platform-fee ownership.
closures.why_root_cause: Each cited backend requirement remains verified; only its current frontend consumer field disagreed with the generated 160-page inventory.
closures.correct_fix: Point payment, compensation and payout/query claims to their canonical UI-12 routes and remove only the retired Finance platform-fee frontend claim while preserving the surviving platform/merchant/branch/audit surfaces.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; focused traceability passed 15 tests and 20 assertions and no retired Finance route remains in the CSV.

closures.observed_problem: Larastan rejected the first UI-12 read-model/resource annotations with 23 errors.
closures.evidence: The level-8 run identified invariant collection generics, an eager-load callback signature and nullable relationship access only in four new UI-12 PHP files.
closures.root_cause: The initial annotations were narrower than Laravel's generic relation contracts and did not express database-enforced relationship integrity to static analysis.
closures.why_root_cause: Generic-safe mapping, resource-side ordering and explicit integrity failures removed every error while the focused API assertions remained unchanged.
closures.correct_fix: Use a method template for model collections, return an explicit list, avoid the incompatible eager-load callback, and fail explicitly if mandatory payment-group relationships are absent.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; Larastan passed 1,462 analysis units with zero errors and the Finance API passed 4 tests/52 assertions.

closures.observed_problem: The first authoritative backend suite ended with two OpenAPI byte-parity failures after 2,983 passing tests.
closures.evidence: The generator inferred precise money-array item shapes and nullable invoice numbers from the Larastan-safe annotations while the committed document retained the earlier weaker schemas.
closures.root_cause: Static-contract corrections intentionally improved Scramble's schema inference after the prior OpenAPI generation boundary.
closures.why_root_cause: Regeneration kept the route count fixed at 296 paths/347 operations, and the focused OpenAPI suite then passed byte equality and production-route coverage.
closures.correct_fix: Regenerate the authoritative OpenAPI document and TypeScript projection from final PHP annotations and prove byte determinism.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the focused OpenAPI suite passed 9 tests/15 assertions.

closures.observed_problem: The backend rerun passed 2,984 tests but the immutable UI-01 audit rejected the removed Finance platform-fee screen as unregistered.
closures.evidence: Ui01AuditContractTest named only finance-platform-fees; UI-12's exact 24-page contract has no Finance platform-fee destination and explicitly records no alias.
closures.root_cause: UI-12 correctly removed the runtime inventory entry but had not added the removal to UI-01's append-only reconciliation register.
closures.why_root_cause: Registering the exact key with UI-12 authority satisfied the frozen-audit invariant while the resurrection guard ensures it cannot silently return.
closures.correct_fix: Record finance-platform-fees as removed by canonical Finance authority with the UI-12 route-activation matrix as evidence.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the focused audit passed 15 tests/2,145 assertions. The correction is test/evidence-only and does not invalidate the 2,984 passing backend results.

closures.observed_problem: The first full frontend run failed seven cases after lint/typecheck: two stale generated snapshots, one orphaned retired screen spec and four UI-01 render timeouts.
closures.evidence: Snapshot diffs exactly matched the finalized Finance contract; screenInventory named only finance/finance-platform-fees.md; the four render cases all passed focused with the slowest at 2.8 seconds under the unchanged five-second budget.
closures.root_cause: The source registers were current but their deterministic YAML fixtures and retired generated spec were not reconciled, while the unconstrained full Vitest worker pool exhausted the local per-case transform budget.
closures.why_root_cause: Regenerating only the snapshots and deleting the authority-retired orphan removed the contract failures; the unchanged render tests passed focused and the full suite passed under a two-worker cap.
closures.correct_fix: Regenerate both derived YAML fixtures, remove the orphaned platform-fee spec, and use a resource-safe two-worker full Vitest invocation without increasing or weakening any test timeout.
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; 141 files/1,390 tests and the 1,299-module production build passed.

closures.observed_problem: The first authoritative whole-product browser run denied two legitimate Finance states: a download-only export user landed on the public page, and a Finance user without liability-view permission could not reach the component's safe no-access state.
closures.evidence: finance-export.spec.ts could not find export-download and phase-20g.spec.ts could not find liability-no-permission; the run ended 1,453 passed / 8 failed / 1,461 collected.
closures.root_cause: The canonical Exports route required finance_export.create even though create and download are independent active capabilities, while the liabilities route guard redirected before the page could render its existing permission-safe state.
closures.why_root_cause: Both failures occurred before the target component behavior: admitting either export capability rendered the existing download-only controls, and allowing the liabilities component to own its UX denial rendered the tested no-permission state without widening any API authority.
closures.correct_fix: Add an explicit any-permission route guard for the independent export capabilities and remove only the redundant liabilities route permission guard; retain the account/active-merchant guards and all server policies/permission middleware.
tests: permissionRouteGuard.spec.ts and affected Finance component/router Vitest: 22/22
focused eight-failure Playwright selection: seven passed before the single release-audit consumer correction
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; no permission key or grant changed and the API remains the security boundary.

closures.observed_problem: Six cases in the first whole-product run encoded pre-UI-12 Finance headings, ownership or route-collision assumptions.
closures.evidence: The failures named Payment recordings, the retired /finance/platform-fees destination, one release-audit key and three wrong-host /dashboard probes after Finance activated its canonical /dashboard.
closures.root_cause: Historical browser consumers had not been reconciled to the binding UI-12 contract: Payment records is the canonical heading, Finance platform-fee ownership is retired with no alias, the inventory uses finance-payment-records-detail, and /dashboard is intentionally owned independently on multiple account hosts.
closures.why_root_cause: Each assertion failed against the correctly selected account router while the target security property remained provable through account-unique routes or the current inventory key.
closures.correct_fix: Update only the superseded labels/keys, assert the retired Finance platform-fee path is absent, and use real account-unique predecessor routes for wrong-host non-disclosure checks; no denial assertion or role boundary was weakened.
tests: focused eight-failure Playwright selection: 7/8 then release-audit focused correction 1/1
closures.remaining_risk: None observed; the final full matrix passed with all cross-account negatives intact.

closures.observed_problem: A filesystem-mode gitleaks scan reported one generic-api-key candidate and stopped the chained security/integrity command.
closures.evidence: The only finding was resources/spa/src/design-system/tokens.generated.ts:13, DESIGN_TOKEN_SOURCE_SHA256, unchanged from main and already documented as a reproducible design-token content digest.
closures.root_cause: Filesystem mode has no commit in its fingerprint, so it cannot match the repository's exact commit-scoped false-positive entries for the unchanged high-entropy SHA-256 digest.
closures.why_root_cause: The value recomputes from committed tokens.json, authenticates nothing, and both pre-commit-diff and full-history gitleaks modes used by repository governance reported zero leaks.
closures.correct_fix: Make no source or scanner-suppression change; record the stopped diagnostic scan and run the scope-correct pre-commit and full-history scans, both of which passed without weakening rules.
closures.remaining_risk: The known content digest can recur under directory-only scanning; CI's commit scan remains authoritative and exact-fingerprint scoped.

closures.observed_problem: The first post-run restoration pass covered the classified frontend audit directories but final Git scope review showed that Playwright had also rewritten predecessor proof under docs/proof/ui-01 and docs/proof/ui-06 and created new UI-01 screenshots there.
closures.evidence: Git identified 10 changed tracked predecessor proof files and 112 untracked screenshots with the exact --dc74e28.png run suffix outside the 250-file frozen audit baseline.
closures.root_cause: The pre-run classification enumerated browser-written audit directories but omitted the separate docs/proof targets written by predecessor E2E suites; directory names alone did not reveal every browser output target.
closures.why_root_cause: Every omitted change was produced by the whole-product run, all 112 additions shared its base-SHA suffix, and no status entry remained after restoring only the 10 individually proven tracked paths and deleting only those 112 validated additions.
closures.correct_fix: Restore the 10 exact tracked paths from the verified base, remove the 112 exact accidental screenshot additions after repository-root and suffix validation, preserve UI-06/UI-07 current projections and UI-12 proof, and extend the evidence record with counts and aggregate hashes.
tests: git status --porcelain=v1 -- docs/proof/ui-01 docs/proof/ui-06: zero entries
10 restored files aggregate SHA-256 684d502297792446ee2339b186be69c3de67179b7d30ef3b44324ec269e3832e and zero diff from HEAD
UI-12 deterministic evidence checker after documentation update
closures.remaining_risk: The original pre-run baseline did not hash these 10 files; their restored state is instead proven against the verified base commit and the omission is retained explicitly rather than retroactively rewriting the baseline.
